Suppose that assumptions (2.2), (2.3) are satisﬁed.
In the non-critical situation |γ| ̸= 1, the singular case occurs if σ > 1.

In the critical situation where |γ| = 1 but τ ̸= 0, the singular case occurs if

self-adjoint extensions of J0 are discrete. Surprisingly, this is, in general, no longer

Abstract: Our goal is to ﬁnd an asymptotic behavior as n →∞of the orthog- onal polynomials Pn(z) deﬁned by Jacobi recurrence coeﬃcients an (oﬀ-diagonal terms) and bn (diagonal terms). We consider the case an →∞, bn →∞in such a way that P a−1 n < ∞(that is, the Carleman condition is violated) and γn := 2−1bn(anan−1)−1/2 →γ as n →∞. In the case |γ| ̸= 1 asymptotic formulas for Pn(z) are known; they depend crucially on the sign of |γ| −1. We study the critical case |γ| = 1. The formulas obtained are qualitatively diﬀerent in the cases |γn| →1 −0 and |γn| →1 + 0. Another goal of the paper is to advocate an approach to a study of asymptotic behavior of Pn(z) based on a close analogy of the Jacobi diﬀerence equations and diﬀerential equations of Schr¨odinger type.
